summary: André proves Hochster's direct summand conjecture: every finite extension of a Noetherian regular ring splits (0.1.1), through Hochster's reduction to W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]] (0.2.1). He also proves that every Noetherian local ring has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra (0.7.1), that finite covers of regular rings are dominated by faithfully flat algebras (0.7.2) and a Cohen–Macaulay descent theorem for pure maps to regular rings with separable residue extension (4.4.2). The key new inputs are the almost faithful flatness of the normalized Kummer tower Â°_∞∞ over A°_∞0 (2.5.2), proved by thickening along tubular neighbourhoods of T = g and descending to Noetherian stages, and a fragment of the companion's perfectoid Abhyankar lemma (3.2.1). The annihilator Lemma 1.1.2 and an Artinian Mittag–Leffler argument then turn almost statements modulo p^m into an honest retraction. The atlas plans the perfectoid and almost-mathematics foundations (PerfectoidSpaces P0–P2), finite depth and Cohen–Macaulay theory (R03.3) and flatness of rational localisations (Tau Ceti AdicSpaces). It lacks ordinary purity, the direct-summand and big-Cohen–Macaulay direction, Hochster's modifications, coherent rings, Cohen structure and the Kummer-tower ramification theory. These are routed to a new DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay roadmap and to the PerfectoidRamification Part II already proposed by the companion. The extraction is complete: 188 items, every missing item routed once, 24 recorded source findings awaiting review (among them an error in the proof of 0.7.2 with its repair, E20, and the appendix duality problems E4, E5 and E21).

items.name: Regular local ring
items.statement: A commutative Noetherian local ring R is regular when its maximal ideal has minimal number of generators equal to dim R.
items.note: Inherited statement check: Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean:51. Local-to-global regularity is a separate theorem.

api.name: IsRegularLocalRing
api.statement: Use the existing class with locality, Noetherianity and the generator/dimension equality.

uses.how: Uses the existing regular-local carrier, not a second private definition.

items.name: Regular ring
items.statement: A commutative Noetherian ring R is regular when R_P is regular local for every prime P.
items.note: Inherited check: Mathlib/RingTheory/RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean:96. Bounded global dimension is not built into this definition.

api.statement: Regularity is tested at every prime localization.

uses.how: Supplies the local regularity hypotheses for the global theorem.

items.name: Weakly regular module sequence
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and R-module M, a finite sequence x is weakly regular when multiplication by x_i is injective on M/(x_1,…,x_{i−1})M for each i.
items.note: Inherited check: Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/RegularSequence.lean:135. There is no finite-generation hypothesis on M.

api.name: RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular
api.statement: Use injectivity on each preceding quotient.

api.name: RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular.of_flat_of_isBaseChange

uses.how: Supplies the regularity condition on possibly infinite modules.

items.name: Regular module sequence
items.statement: A weakly regular sequence x on M is regular if M/(x)M is nonzero.
items.note: Inherited check: Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/RegularSequence.lean:146. Big CM additionally imposes m_B C≠C.

api.name: RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular
api.statement: Weak regularity and nonzero final quotient.

api.statement: The sequence ideal does not generate the whole module.

items.name: Faithfully flat module
items.statement: An R-module M is faithfully flat if it is flat and mM≠M for every maximal ideal m of R; equivalently its tensor functor is exact and faithful.
items.note: Inherited check: Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat/Basic.lean:63,73.

api.name: Module.FaithfullyFlat.iff_flat_and_proper_ideal
api.statement: Flatness plus properness of all extended proper ideals.

api.name: Module.FaithfullyFlat.one_tmul_eq_zero_iff
api.statement: Faithful algebra base change detects an element being zero.

uses.how: Distinguishes faithful flatness from generic or almost flatness.

items.name: Unit tensor map of a faithfully flat algebra
items.statement: If S is a faithfully flat R-algebra and M is any R-module, 1⊗m=0 in S⊗_R M iff m=0.
items.note: Inherited actual-statement check: Basic.lean:482. This supplies tensor injectivity, not a generic named purity predicate.

items.name: Weak regularity under flat base change
items.statement: If R→S is flat and x is weakly regular on an R-module M, its image is weakly regular on S⊗_R M.
items.note: Inherited check: Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/Flat.lean:34, with arbitrary-module generality.

items.name: Completion of the Noetherian base is flat
items.statement: For a commutative Noetherian ring R and ideal I, its I-adic completion is R-flat.
items.locator: Special case S=R of Lemma 1.1.1, p.75
items.note: Inherited check: Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/AsTensorProduct.lean:379. This does not give completion flatness of an arbitrary non-Noetherian R-flat algebra S.

items.name: Witt vectors of a perfect field form a DVR
items.statement: If p is prime and k is a perfect field of characteristic p, W_p(k) is a discrete valuation ring.
items.note: Inherited check: Mathlib/RingTheory/WittVector/DiscreteValuationRing.lean:149. Completeness and coefficient-ring reduction are separate inputs.

items.name: Pure module monomorphism
items.statement: An R-linear injection M→N is pure if P⊗_R M→P⊗_R N is injective for every R-module P.
items.note: Follow Mathlib PR #22909 at c2ab6bbf5e75dfa6ab145d538e276a883e0af724: Submodule.IsPure on the image of an injection, with an explicit all-module tensor characterization. The PR was open in the predecessor check and is not pinned coverage. No competing PureLinearMap carrier is proposed.

api.name: Submodule.IsPure.iff_fp_tensor

api.name: Submodule.IsPure.baseChange_injective

uses.how: Provides the ordinary tensor-injectivity predicate and its lifting interface.

items.name: Pure ring homomorphism
items.statement: A homomorphism f:R→S of commutative unital rings is pure if M→S⊗_R M, m↦1⊗m, is injective for every R-module M. In particular f is injective.

api.name: PureRingHom.tensor_unit_injective

api.name: PureRingHom.baseChange

api.name: PureRingHom.of_comp
api.statement: A pure composite has a pure first factor.

uses.how: Supplies tensor injectivity, not the radicial scheme-morphism notion.

items.name: Generator module
items.statement: An R-module M is a generator if every R-module N is generated by the union of the images of all R-linear maps M→N.

api.name: ModuleGenerator.iff_finite_power_summand
api.statement: R is a summand of some finite power of M.

api.name: ModuleGenerator.eval_family
api.statement: Produce finitely many m_i and λ_i:M→R with Σλ_i(m_i)=1.

api.name: ModuleGenerator.of_linearEquiv
api.statement: Transport under R-linear equivalence.

items.name: Linear splitting of an algebra map
items.statement: For an R-algebra S, a splitting is an R-linear map ρ:S→R with ρ(1)=1, equivalently ρ composed with R→S is the identity. Multiplicativity is not required.

api.name: AlgebraSplitting.retract_one
api.statement: For R-linear ρ, ρ∘algebraMap=id iff ρ(1)=1.

api.name: AlgebraSplitting.baseChange
api.statement: Tensor a splitting with any R-algebra.

api.name: AlgebraSplitting.kerDecomposition
api.statement: S≅R⊕kerρ as R-modules.

uses.how: Expresses the linear, rather than algebra, retraction target.

items.name: Finite-presentation test for module purity
items.statement: An R-linear injection is pure iff tensoring with every finitely presented R-module preserves injectivity.

items.name: Lazard lifting criterion
items.statement: For M⊂N, purity is equivalent to surjectivity of Hom_R(P,N)→Hom_R(P,N/M) for every finitely presented R-module P.

items.name: Pure inclusion with finitely presented quotient splits
items.statement: If N/M is finitely presented, M⊂N is pure iff it admits an R-linear retraction.

items.name: Purity as filtered colimit of split monomorphisms
items.statement: A module monomorphism is pure iff it is a filtered colimit, in the arrow category of R-modules, of split monomorphisms.

items.name: Pure inclusions remain injective on Tor
items.statement: For a pure inclusion M⊂N, any R-module P and every i≥0, Tor_i^R(P,M)→Tor_i^R(P,N) is injective.

items.name: Purity inside a flat module
items.statement: If N is R-flat, M⊂N is pure iff N/M is R-flat.

items.name: Restriction of scalars preserves module purity
items.statement: If S is a commutative R-algebra, every pure map of S-modules is pure as a map of R-modules.

items.name: Finite-power criterion for a generator
items.statement: M is an R-module generator iff R is an R-linear direct summand of M^n for some finite n.

items.name: Purity as injectivity after algebra base change
items.statement: R→S is pure iff R′→S⊗_R R′ is injective for every commutative R-algebra R′; finitely presented R-algebras suffice.
items.note: Use Sym_R(P) and its degree-one summand. This is not the radicial/universally injective scheme-morphism predicate.

items.name: Composition of pure algebra maps
items.statement: If R→S and S→T are pure, R→T is pure.

items.name: Base change of pure algebra maps
items.statement: If R→S is pure, R′→R′⊗_R S is pure for every R-algebra R′.

items.name: Filtered colimits preserve pure maps
items.statement: A filtered colimit of compatible pure homomorphisms of commutative rings is pure.

items.name: A pure composite has pure first factor
items.statement: If R→S→T has pure composite, R→S is pure.

items.name: Flatness descends through a pure second factor
items.statement: If R→S→T has R-flat T and pure S→T, then S is R-flat.

items.name: Purity is faithfulness of extension of scalars
items.statement: R→S is pure iff extension of scalars Mod_R→Mod_S is faithful.

items.name: Faithfully flat is flat and pure
items.statement: R→S is faithfully flat iff it is both flat and pure.

items.name: Finite-presentation splitting criterion for algebras
items.statement: If S is finitely presented as an R-module, the conditions that R→S is pure, that it splits R-linearly, and that S is an R-module generator are equivalent.
items.note: Use Hom_R(S,R), correcting E1. For generator⇒split choose a finite family λ_i,s_i with Σλ_i(s_i)=1 and put ρ(t)=Σλ_i(s_i t); do not assume a single chosen evaluation is 1.

items.name: Purity survives local Noetherian completion
items.statement: If R→S is a pure local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, the induced map between their maximal-ideal-adic completions is pure.
items.note: The completed-base module test and the proof’s completion/descent step remain G5. Do not substitute arbitrary non-Noetherian completion.

items.name: Completion of a flat algebra over a Noetherian base
items.statement: Let R be commutative Noetherian, I an ideal, and S an R-flat commutative R-algebra, not necessarily Noetherian or I-adically separated. The separated I-adic completion of S is R-flat.

items.name: Finite-module tensor commutes with completion of a flat algebra
items.statement: Under Lemma 1.1.1, for every finite R-module M, the canonical map M⊗_R Ŝ→lim_n (M⊗_R S)/I^n(M⊗_R S) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Faithfulness after completion
items.statement: Under Lemma 1.1.1, if S is faithfully flat and I⊆Jac(R), then its separated I-adic completion is faithfully flat over R.

items.name: Contracting an idempotent annihilator
items.statement: Let R be Noetherian, M finite over R, S faithfully flat over R, and K⊂S an ideal with K²=K and K(M⊗_R S)=0. For every s∈R whose image lies in K, there is r∈Ann_R(M) with (1−r)s=0.

items.name: Local annihilator vanishing
items.statement: In Lemma 1.1.2, if R is local and the contraction of K to R is nonzero, then M=0.
items.note: A nonzero contraction suffices even when its element is a zero divisor: if M≠0, Ann(M)⊂m and 1−r is a unit.

items.name: Almost base and almost-zero modules
items.statement: An almost base is a commutative ring V with an idempotent ideal m for which m⊗_V m is V-flat. A V-module M is almost zero when mM=0; almostification is the Serre quotient by these modules.
items.note: Import the generic carrier, not a valuation-only substitute. Companion PAPER-ANDRE-18 §1 is a shared supplier.

api.name: AlmostBase.ideal_idempotent
api.statement: Expose m²=m and flatness of m⊗_V m.

api.name: AlmostZero.annihilated
api.statement: Every element of m annihilates the module.

api.name: AlmostBase.change
api.statement: Compare relative categories after checking the generated-ideal condition.

uses.how: Provides the generic base used by both valuation and ramified almost mathematics.

items.name: Exact tensor-compatible left adjoint for almost modules
items.statement: For the almost base (V,m), the left adjoint M↦M_! to almostification is exact and commutes with tensor products; it is given by (m⊗_V m)⊗_V M_*.
items.note: Cited Gabber–Ramero 2.2.24 and 2.4.35. The module ! and algebra !! are distinct.

items.name: Almost pure module map
items.statement: Over a fixed almost base (V,m) and a V-algebra R, an R-linear map M→N is almost pure if ker(P⊗_R M→P⊗_R N) is annihilated by m for every R-module P.
items.note: This concrete predicate does not require literal injectivity. A.4.1 additionally starts with M⊂N.

api.name: AlmostPureLinearMap.tensor_kernel
api.statement: The fixed base ideal kills every tensor kernel.

api.name: AlmostPureLinearMap.iff_leftAdjoint
api.statement: Compare with ordinary purity after !.

api.name: AlmostPureLinearMap.ordinary
api.statement: Ordinary purity implies almost purity for every admissible almost base.

uses.how: Expresses almost injectivity for all tensor tests.

items.name: Almost purity tested through the module left adjoint
items.statement: An R-linear map is almost pure iff its map M^a_!→N^a_! is a pure module monomorphism.
items.note: Import ordinary purity from the commutative-algebra prefix and almost adjoints from P0.

items.name: Almost lifting for finitely presented modules
items.statement: If M⊂N is almost pure and P is finitely presented over R in the ordinary sense, Hom_R(P,N)→Hom_R(P,N/M) has almost-zero cokernel.

items.name: Almost purity annihilates a finite-presentation extension class
items.statement: For an almost pure inclusion M⊂N with N/M finitely presented as an ordinary R-module, every η∈m kills the class of 0→M→N→N/M→0 in Ext_R^1(N/M,M).
items.note: For each η lift η·id_(N/M). No single ordinary splitting is asserted.

items.name: Almost pure algebra maps and the algebra left adjoint
items.statement: A map R→S of V-algebras is almost pure as an R-module map iff R^a_!!→S^a_!! is a pure ring map.
items.note: Retain the algebra left adjoint !!, not the module functor !.

items.name: Almost purity of the first factor
items.statement: If R→S→T is almost pure as a composite of V-algebra maps, then R→S is almost pure.

items.name: Faithful flatness through the algebra left adjoint
items.statement: For a map of almost algebras over an admissible almost base, faithful flatness is equivalent to ordinary faithful flatness of the map obtained using the algebra left adjoint !!.
items.note: Import PAPER-ANDRE-18/1.6-flatness-transport. Source check (cc-442dc5): Gabber–Ramero arXiv:math/0201175v3 Remark 3.1.3(ii): A ↦ A_!! does not preserve flatness in general, but preserves faithful flatness (φ is a monomorphism iff φ_!! is injective, and B_!!/A_!! ≅ B_!/A_!, flat over A_!! iff B/A is flat over A).

items.name: Reframing by an ideal with the same generated image
items.statement: Changing the almost base along V→V′ gives the same relative almost-module category on an algebra R when both base ideals generate the same ideal of R.
items.note: Import PAPER-ANDRE-18/1.5-reframing; each application proves equality of generated ideals, not just containment.

items.name: Completed cyclotomic Witt-fraction field is perfectoid
items.statement: For perfect k of characteristic p, let K_0=Frac(W(k)), choose compatible primitive p^j-th roots ζ_(p^j), and put K_∞=∪_j K_0(ζ_(p^j)). Its valuation completion is a perfectoid field.
items.note: k need not be finite. The locally compact local-field setting does not supply this entire assertion.

items.name: Integral model of a perfectoid Weierstrass localization
items.statement: Let C be a spectral perfectoid algebra over a perfectoid field and let f,ϖ admit compatible p-power roots, with ϖ a pseudouniformizer and f power bounded. The canonical map from the ϖ-adic completion of C°[(f/ϖ^i)^(1/p^∞)] to C{f/ϖ^i}° is an almost isomorphism for the valuation almost ideal.
items.note: The cited input is Scholze 2012 Lemma 6.4(ii), read in the published version (p.281): for U = U(f_1,…,f_n/g) ⊆ Spa(R^♭, R^(♭+)) rational with f_i, g ∈ R^(♭°) and f_n = ϖ^(♭N), O_X(U)°^a = R°⟨(f_1^♯/g^♯)^(1/p^∞),…,(f_n^♯/g^♯)^(1/p^∞)⟩^a. André applies it to numerators f_i^♭, ϖ^(♭i) and denominator ϖ^(♭i). This is why f_i must be an untilt (tube-sharp-approximation). The conclusion is an almost isomorphism, not an equality of integral rings.

items.name: Normalized two-index Kummer tower
items.statement: Fix perfect k of characteristic p, A=W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]], 0≠g∈A, and compatible cyclotomic and coordinate roots. For finite j,k define A_jk=K_j°[[T_1^(1/p^j),…,T_n^(1/p^j)]][U]/(U^(p^k)−g)[1/p]; let A_jk° be the integral closure of A in A_jk. Infinite indices mean directed unions; hats mean separated p-adic completion of the integral ring, followed on the generic algebra by inverting p.
items.note: The adjoining-root quotient is not silently identified with its normalization A_jk°. For k>0 even A_jk need not be a domain.

api.name: NormalizedKummerTower.level
api.statement: Expose the algebra, normal integral model and structure map at (j,k).

api.name: NormalizedKummerTower.transition
api.statement: Compatible cyclotomic, coordinate and g roots give transitions with identity and composition laws.

api.name: NormalizedKummerTower.complete
api.statement: Distinguish the integral union, separated p-adic completion and generic fibre.

uses.how: Supplies the specified normalized extension whose almost flatness is proved.

items.name: Faithful flatness before adjoining the ramifying root
items.statement: A_j0°=K_j°[[T_1^(1/p^j),…,T_n^(1/p^j)]]. Its finite transition maps and A→A_j0° are finite faithfully flat. A_∞0° and its p-adic completion are faithfully flat over A and over every finite stage.
items.note: Check completion over each Noetherian finite stage via 1.1.1, not by assuming the union A_∞0° Noetherian.

items.name: Normalized root tower as completed tubular colimit
items.statement: For the tower above, C=Â_∞0 and a pseudouniformizer ϖ of the completed K_∞, Â_∞∞°^a is canonically isomorphic to the completed colimit over i of (C〈U^(1/p^∞)〉{(U−g)/ϖ^i})°^a in the valuation almost base (K_∞°,K_∞°°).
items.note: Reuse PAPER-ANDRE-18/2.9.3-root-as-colimit in PerfectoidRamification with an explicit normalization/completion adapter, not a second generic root algebra. The companion's Corollary 2.9.3 (formula (2.32)) was read in the published version, p.34: ucolim_i A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩{(T−g)/ϖ^i}^u ≅ A⟨g^(1/p^∞)⟩ with the unit-ball form ((colim_i …°)^)_* ≅ A⟨g^(1/p^∞)⟩°.

items.name: André’s normalized Kummer almost faithful flatness
items.statement: For the normalized tower, Â_∞∞° is almost faithfully flat over A_∞0° in the valuation almost base (K_∞°,K_∞°°).
items.note: The almost ideal here does not involve g. This specified extension is not identified without proof with the existential cover in PerfectoidQuotients:Q3. Proof spine (cc-442dc5): coordinate-tower-perfectoid; tube-sharp-approximation (Scholze 6.7(i)); root-localisation-colimit (Scholze 6.4); noetherian-stage-model; flatness-by-fibres with generic-fibre-flat and special-fibre-free; noetherian-stage-faithfully-flat; colimit-base-flatness and faithful-completion; tube-almost-faithfully-flat; one more completed colimit over i and kummer-tube-comparison.

items.name: Purity of the finite normalized Kummer extensions
items.statement: For every finite pair (j,k) in the tower, A_j0°→A_jk° is pure.
items.note: Needs coherence of the finite-flat union, finite-presentation descent of annihilators and 1.1.2; almost injectivity alone is insufficient. Proof checked (cc-442dc5): N ⊆ ker(P → P ⊗ A°_∞∞) is finitely presented because A°_∞0 is coherent; its annihilator I is finitely generated, contains K°°_∞ and descends to I_j ⊂ A°_j0; Lemma 1.1.2 with K = A°°_∞0, which meets A°_j0 in a nonzero ideal, gives I_j = A°_j0.

items.name: Ordinary faithful flatness on generic fibres
items.statement: Â_∞∞ is faithfully flat over A_∞0 and hence over A[1/p]. In particular nonzero g∈A is a nonzerodivisor on Â_∞∞.
items.note: Inverting p kills valuation-almost-zero modules. This does not assert ordinary integral faithful flatness.

items.name: Faithfully flat algebra left-adjoint model
items.statement: Set C°=Â_∞∞°. Relative to (A_∞0°,K_∞°°A_∞0°), the algebra left adjoint S=(C°^a)_!! identifies with the subalgebra A_∞0°+K_∞°°C° of C°. It is faithfully flat over A_∞0° and A.
items.note: S contains and is stable under multiplication by (ϖg)^(1/p^h); this does not say that it contains each g-root separately. Source check (cc-442dc5): in Gabber–Ramero arXiv v3, B_!! is defined in 2.2.23 by the right-exact sequence (2.2.24) 0 → m̃ → V ⊕ B_! → B_!! → 0, exact when m̃ ≅ m (Remark 2.2.26); André's ‘formule (2.2.26)’ is this construction (the LNM numbering was not checked). The map B_!! → B_* is injective here because B_!! is flat and m is a union of principal ideals generated by non-zero-divisors of A°_∞0, which identifies B_!! with A°_∞0 + K°°_∞ Â°_∞∞.

api.name: AndreFlatModel.algebraMap
api.statement: Expose A_∞0°→S and S→C°.

api.name: AndreFlatModel.mem
api.statement: Elements are sums of a base element and an element of K_∞°°C°.

api.name: AndreFlatModel.rootIdeal
api.statement: Each (ϖg)^(1/p^h) preserves S and acts on its reduction modulo p^m.

uses.how: Replaces valuation-almost flatness by an actual flat algebra before annihilator descent.

items.name: Integral closure used for a finite extension
items.statement: Let A→B be a finite injection with B reduced and p-torsion-free, and choose g∈A outside pA such that B[1/(pg)] is finite étale over A[1/(pg)]. With C=Â_∞∞, let D be the integral closure of C° in B⊗_A C[1/g]. The canonical map B⊗_A S→B⊗_A C[1/g] factors through D.
items.note: Reuse the companion’s ramified normalization. Do not identify B⊗S with a normal or finite-étale integral algebra.

api.name: RamifiedIntegralModel.map
api.statement: Factor B⊗_A S through D by integrality.

api.name: RamifiedIntegralModel.integral
api.statement: Every element is integral over C° in the stated ambient generic algebra.

api.name: RamifiedIntegralModel.generic
api.statement: After inverting pg, compare with B⊗_A C[1/g].

uses.how: Supplies the integral ramified target for almost purity and almost CM.

items.name: Ramified almost faithful flatness modulo p powers
items.statement: In the preceding setup, C°/p^m→D/p^m is almost faithfully flat, hence almost pure, for every m≥1, in the base (K_∞°[U^(1/p^∞)],U^(1/p^∞)K_∞°°[U^(1/p^∞)]) acting by U^(1/p^h)↦g^(1/p^h).
items.note: Import the companion's Theorem 0.3.1 (published pp.2–3, read): (1) B° is almost the integral closure of g^(−1/p^∞)A° in B′, (2) B°/p^m is almost finite étale over A°/p^m, (3) the trace is almost surjective onto g^(−1/p^∞)A° when B′ is faithful. Faithful flatness, which 0.3.1 does not state, is abhyankar-faithfulness; footnote 4 (the Galois case suffices) is galois-closure-reduction.

items.name: Almost purity after passing to the actual flat model
items.statement: For S above and every m≥1, S/p^m→(B⊗_A S)/p^m is almost pure in the base (K_∞°+K_∞°°[U^(1/p^∞)],U^(1/p^∞)K_∞°°[U^(1/p^∞)]) with U-roots acting through g-roots.
items.note: The smaller base matters because S need not contain all g-roots. Reframe and use the factorization through D/p^m.

items.name: Ext base change for the finite splitting obstruction
items.statement: If R is Noetherian, Q finite over R, and S R-flat, the natural map Ext_R^1(Q,R)⊗_R S→Ext_S^1(Q⊗_R S,S) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Use a finite-free resolution through the required degrees. Finite presentation alone over a non-Noetherian ring is not this hypothesis.

items.name: Vanishing of the splitting obstruction modulo p powers
items.statement: For a finite extension A⊂B of A=W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]] with perfect k of characteristic p, A/p^m→B/p^m admits an A/p^m-linear retraction for every m≥1.
items.note: After reduction to a reduced p-torsion-free extension, use m≥2, R=A/p^m, finite cyclic M=Re, faithfully flat S/p^m and the idempotent ramified root ideal. Its contraction contains nonzero pg modulo p^m. Obtain m=1 by reduction.

items.name: Recovering an integral splitting from Artinian quotients
items.statement: For finite A⊂B with A=W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]], splittings modulo every I_m=(p^m,T_1^(p^m),…,T_n^(p^m)), m≥1, imply an A-linear splitting A→B.
items.note: Source proof now checked: use cosets in Artinian modules, stabilize their images, restrict to eventual ranges and choose a compatible sequence. Artinian does not mean a finite underlying set when k is infinite. Original transition maps need not be surjective. Completeness of finite B is unnecessary for the last step: Hom_A(B,−) commutes with the target inverse limit.

items.name: Direct summand theorem for the unramified complete local base
items.statement: Let k be perfect of characteristic p and A=W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]]. Every module-finite injective commutative A-algebra B admits an A-linear retraction to A.

items.name: Direct summand theorem
items.statement: For every commutative Noetherian regular ring R and commutative R-algebra S that is faithful and finite as an R-module, R→S admits an R-linear retraction.
items.note: Hochster 1983 Theorem 6.1(2⇒1) is now source-read and recorded as unramified-reduction; G3 retains its unextracted intermediate suppliers rather than misattributing it to the 1973 Artinian-limit argument.

items.name: Big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for a chosen parameter system
items.statement: Let (B,m_B) be Noetherian local of dimension d, x=(x_1,…,x_d) a system of parameters and C a commutative B-algebra not assumed Noetherian. C is big Cohen–Macaulay for (B,x) if m_B C≠C and x is C-regular.
items.note: Reuse the pinned regular-sequence predicate on the B-module C; no finite B-module condition on C.

api.name: BigCMFor.regular
api.statement: Extract regularity of the specified parameter list.

api.name: BigCMFor.residue_nonzero
api.statement: Extract C/m_B C≠0.

api.name: BigCMFor.equiv
api.statement: Transport across B-algebra equivalences preserving the chosen parameters.

uses.how: Specifies the initial chosen-parameter algebra before balancing.

items.name: Balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra
items.statement: For Noetherian local B, a B-algebra C is balanced big Cohen–Macaulay if it is big Cohen–Macaulay for every system of parameters of B.

api.name: BalancedBigCM.for_parameters
api.statement: Specialize to each parameter system of B.

api.name: BalancedBigCM.equiv
api.statement: Transport across B-algebra equivalences.

api.name: BalancedBigCM.not_finite_required
api.statement: The predicate applies to all B-algebras without finite-module or Noetherian hypotheses on C.

uses.how: Supplies regularity for every parameter system in the existence theorem.

items.name: Almost big Cohen–Macaulay algebra
items.statement: Fix Noetherian local B of residue characteristic p, a parameter system x and a B-algebra D with a nonzerodivisor π and compatible elements π_h satisfying π_0=π and π_(h+1)^p=π_h. Put J=Σ_h π_h D. D is almost big CM for this data if J⊄m_B D and J annihilates ((x_1,…,x_i)D:x_(i+1))/(x_1,…,x_i)D for every 0≤i<dim B.
items.note: J⊄m_B D is stronger than D≠m_B D. J is idempotent; π need not equal p.

api.name: AlmostBigCM.rootIdeal
api.statement: Expose J=Σ_h π_hD and J²=J.

api.name: AlmostBigCM.colon_annihilated
api.statement: J kills each specified colon quotient.

api.name: AlmostBigCM.residue_not_almost_zero
api.statement: J⊄m_BD, with a root-element witness.

api.name: AlmostBigCM.change_roots
api.statement: Changing compatible roots without changing J preserves the almost regularity and nontriviality conditions.

uses.how: Records colon annihilation and non-almost-zero residue separately.

items.name: Almost big CM implies existence of balanced big CM
items.statement: If a Noetherian local ring B of residue characteristic p has an almost big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for one parameter system and a compatible root system of a nonzerodivisor, then B admits a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra.
items.note: Proof: almost-cm-no-bad-sequence, then no-bad-sequence-criterion gives C_x(B), then completion-balances. The parenthetical claim that B → D factors through the colimit is not established and not used (E19).

items.name: Almost CM across a finite local base
items.statement: Let A⊂B be a finite extension of Noetherian local rings with A Cohen–Macaulay, and let x⊂A be a system of parameters of B. For a B-algebra D with the standing root/nonzerodivisor data, D is almost big CM for (B,x,π-roots) iff it is so for (A,x,π-roots).

items.name: Almost faithful flatness criterion for almost CM
items.statement: In Lemma 4.1.3, D is almost big CM if (πD)∩A≠0 and D is almost isomorphic to an A-faithfully-flat A-algebra in the base (A[π^(1/p^∞)],π^(1/p^∞)A[π^(1/p^∞)]). The comparison algebra need not contain B.

items.name: Almost CM from faithful flatness modulo the first parameter
items.statement: In Lemma 4.1.3, D is almost big CM if (πD)∩A is not contained in x_1 A, D has no x_1-torsion, and D/x_1D is almost isomorphic in the root-ideal base of (a) to an A/x_1A-faithfully-flat algebra.
items.note: Retain noncontainment modulo x_1 and the standing nonzerodivisor condition on π.

items.name: Existence of balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebras
items.statement: Every commutative Noetherian local ring B has a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra.
items.note: Reductions are big-cm-reductions (minimal prime, completion, nilradical, perfect residue field), cohen-parameter-presentation and discriminant-element; the equal-characteristic case is Hochster's and is a prerequisite.

items.name: Big CM algebras over a regular local base are faithfully flat
items.statement: If A is Noetherian regular local and C is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay A-algebra, C is faithfully flat over A.
items.note: Do not assume C finitely generated. Use bounded projective dimension of finite A-modules and a Tor dimension-shifting argument; finite-module Auslander–Buchsbaum alone does not prove this. The footnote on p.87 prints M where N is required in two Tor terms (E6); the corrected proof explicitly retains the associated-prime embedding supplier.

items.name: Finite extensions of regular rings are dominated by faithfully flat algebras
items.statement: Let R be commutative Noetherian regular and R⊂S a finite extension. There exists a commutative S-algebra T such that R→T is faithfully flat.
items.note: Neither finiteness of T nor S-flatness is asserted. Use only the factors S_(m,i) that receive R̂_m injectively (E20): the printed proof takes all factors, and a factor of smaller dimension has a big CM algebra that is not flat over R̂_m. At least one such factor exists for each m by lying over, so T = ∏ T_(m,i) over these factors is flat by product-flat-noetherian and satisfies mT ≠ T.

items.name: Compatible almost CM data produce compatible big CM algebras
items.statement: For a local map β:B→B′ of complete local domains of mixed characteristic (0,p), suppose B→D, B′→D′ and δ:D→D′ form a commutative square, D and D′ are almost big CM for chosen parameter systems and root systems π_h and π′_h, and δ(π_h) divides π′_h for every h. Then there is a commutative square over β whose vertical targets are balanced big CM algebras C and C′.
items.note: Use B′ in the primed triple (E3). Existential compatibility, not a canonical functor. Proof by the two-ring version of the modification technique: double sequences of partial modifications over β (Heitmann–Ma Theorem 1.6, from Hochster 2002 Theorem 4.2), with hochster-key-lemma applied on both sides and the divisibility δ(π^(1/p^m)) | π′^(1/p^m) to compare denominators.

items.name: CM descent from a regular target in the stated mixed-characteristic range
items.statement: If B→B′ is a pure local extension of Noetherian local rings of mixed characteristic (0,p), B′ is regular, and the residue-field extension is separable, then B is Cohen–Macaulay.
items.note: Proof: complete (purity-perfect-residue, cm-completion); B̂ ⊆ B̂′ is a domain because B̂′ is a regular local ring; weak-functoriality-regular-target gives the square; hh-cm-descent concludes. Keep residue separability, which this proof uses; later work that removes it (§0.8) is not imported.

items.name: Cohen–Macaulay local ring
items.statement: A commutative Noetherian local ring B is Cohen–Macaulay when depth B equals dim B, equivalently when every system of parameters is a regular sequence on B.
items.note: Import shared finite-ring/module CM and depth theory. AUDIT-17 marks it absent in the pin but planned here; do not redeclare it in the big-CM direction.

api.name: IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing.iff_parameter_regular
api.statement: Import the R03.3 parameter-system characterization.

api.name: IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing.depth_eq_dim
api.statement: Import the shared depth convention.

api.name: IsCohenMacaulayLocalRing.quotient_regular
api.statement: Import the CM quotient-by-regular-element theorem with dimension drop.

uses.how: Supplies the ordinary finite CM predicate and parameter characterization.

items.name: Cofinality of André’s Artinian parameter quotients
items.statement: For A=W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]], k perfect of characteristic p, maximal ideal m_A=(p,T_1,…,T_n), and integer m≥1, put I_m=(p^m,T_1^(p^m),…,T_n^(p^m)). Then I_(m+1)⊆I_m and m_A^(m+n(p^m−1))⊆I_m⊆m_A^m. Consequently A/I_m is Artinian and the map A→lim_m A/I_m is an isomorphism.
items.locator: André §3.4, p.84; explicit cofinality calculation for the quotients used there
items.note: Complete Noetherian power-series structure is an inherited foundational input, not newly claimed as an exact pinned declaration; G7 retains that fine audit.

items.name: Mittag–Leffler stabilization of retraction cosets
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian, let I_m be descending ideals with each A/I_m Artinian, let B be a finitely generated A-module and e∈B. Assume H_m={f∈Hom_A(B,A/I_m):f(e)=1} is nonempty for every m≥1. Reduction induces an inverse system H_m. For each m the images of H_l→H_m, l≥m, eventually stabilize.
items.locator: Hochster, Contracted ideals from integral extensions of regular rings (1973), p.30, retraction sets H_k and their images; used by André §3.4
items.note: This is the algebra-specific adapter, not a second definition of Mittag–Leffler systems. Reuse CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler.

items.name: Surjective transitions on eventual ranges
items.statement: For a functor F:J→Type on a cofiltered category satisfying the Mittag–Leffler condition, every transition map of the eventual-range subfunctor is surjective.
items.locator: Generic step in Hochster 1973 p.30 and André §3.4; pinned Mathlib/CategoryTheory/CofilteredSystem.lean, surjective_toEventualRanges
items.note: Read at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. No Finite hypothesis on the types. Do not substitute eval_section_surjective_of_surjective from the later finite-system section.

items.name: Nonempty eventual ranges of a Mittag–Leffler system
items.statement: A pointwise nonempty Mittag–Leffler functor to types on a cofiltered category has a nonempty eventual range at every object.
items.locator: Generic step in Hochster 1973 p.30 and André §3.4; pinned Mathlib/CategoryTheory/CofilteredSystem.lean, toEventualRanges_nonempty
items.note: Read at the pin. Stabilization identifies the eventual range with one actual nonempty image; no compactness or finite-set hypothesis is required.

items.name: Compatible choice in a countable surjective inverse system
items.statement: For nonempty sets E_m, m≥1, and surjective maps q_m:E_(m+1)→E_m, there exist e_m∈E_m with q_m(e_(m+1))=e_m for all m. The first coordinate may be any specified e_1∈E_1.
items.locator: Hochster 1973, p.30, passage from stabilized retraction sets to a compatible system; elementary recursive-choice expansion
items.note: The pinned CofilteredSystem finite-type nonemptiness theorem is not applicable to arbitrary Artinian modules. This elementary adapter needs no independent choice-system carrier; fine library reduction remains part of G7.

items.name: Reconstructing a functional from compatible target quotients
items.statement: Let I_m be descending ideals in a commutative ring A such that A→lim_m A/I_m is an isomorphism. For any A-module B, compatible A-linear maps f_m:B→A/I_m determine a unique A-linear f:B→A whose reductions are the f_m. If e∈B and f_m(e)=1 for every m, then f(e)=1.
items.locator: Hochster 1973 p.30, Hom inverse-limit step; André §3.4
items.note: This does not claim B≅lim B/I_mB. Such a comparison is unnecessary here.

items.name: Corrected contracting-endomorphism functional criterion
items.statement: Let (R,m) be a nonzero commutative local ring, r∈m, and suppose ∩_(n≥1) r^nR=0 and either r=0 or multiplication by r on R is injective. Let σ:R→R be a local endomorphism with R free as a module over σ(R), and suppose ∩_(j≥0) σ^j(m)R⊆rR. Let R⊂S be a commutative ring extension and τ:S→S an injective endomorphism restricting to σ. If Hom_R(S,R)≠0, there is an R-linear ρ:S→R with ρ(1)=1.
items.locator: Appendix A.3.1(c)⇒(b), pp.90–91, with the explicit additional hypothesis required by E4
items.note: This is a corrected sufficient hypothesis, not a claim that it is necessary or that the entire regular/integral (a)⇒(b) part of A.3.1 has been verified. The report supplies the full counterexample and proof. E4 awaits independent review.

items.name: Local cohomology via the Ext colimit
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, ideal I and R-module M, H_I^i(M)=colim_t Ext_R^i(R/I^t,M), with its functorial action on module maps. Reuse the existing localCohomology functor.
items.note: The carrier and radical comparison exist; the Čech/Tor comparison and these computational tests require the missing adapters below. Planning tests are not claimed compiled.

api.name: localCohomology
api.statement: Instantiate the existing functor on I and i.

api.name: localCohomology.map
api.statement: Apply the functor to a linear map, retaining identity and composition.

api.name: localCohomology.isoOfSameRadical
api.statement: Use the pinned radical-invariance comparison over Noetherian R.

uses.how: Carries top local cohomology; no second Čech-only carrier.

items.name: Radical invariance of local cohomology
items.statement: For commutative Noetherian R and ideals I,J with sqrt(I)=sqrt(J), the functors H_I^i and H_J^i on R-modules are naturally isomorphic.

items.name: Tensor–Hom linear equivalence
items.statement: For R-modules M,N,E over commutative R, Hom_R(M,Hom_R(N,E))≅Hom_R(M⊗_R N,E), carrying f to (m⊗n↦f(m)(n)).

items.name: Extension of a map into an injective module
items.statement: If E is an injective R-module, i:M→N an injective R-linear map and g:M→E linear, there is h:N→E with h∘i=g. Keep the Small universe hypothesis of the pinned statement when universes differ.

items.name: Injective envelope predicate
items.statement: An R-linear map k→E is an injective envelope if it is injective, E is an injective R-module, and the image is essential: every nonzero submodule of E meets the image nontrivially. Reuse TauCeti.IsInjectiveEnvelope.
items.locator: André A.3.1; Hochster Local cohomology (2011), §1; pinned TauCeti/Algebra/Module/Injective/Envelope.lean
items.note: Whole pinned file read. Its docstring explicitly does not prove existence; do not count enough injectives as enough injective envelopes.

api.name: TauCeti.IsInjectiveEnvelope.moduleInjective
api.statement: Extract Module.Injective R E.

api.name: TauCeti.IsInjectiveEnvelope.exists_linearEquiv
api.statement: Two envelopes have an R-linear equivalence commuting with the embeddings; retain Small hypotheses.

api.name: TauCeti.isInjectiveEnvelope_id
api.statement: The identity of an injective module is its envelope.

uses.how: Separates the existing predicate/uniqueness from the unbuilt existence theorem.

items.name: Existence of the residue-field injective hull
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R,m,k), there are an R-module E and an R-linear map k→E satisfying TauCeti.IsInjectiveEnvelope.
items.locator: Hochster Local cohomology (2011), Proposition 1.6 and following paragraph, pp.7–8
items.note: Specialization of the existing general envelope direction, with one shared existence proof; do not create a competing envelope carrier or claim general existence is already pinned.

items.name: Endomorphisms of the residue-field injective hull
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring R and E=E_R(R/m), the scalar action induces an isomorphism Rhat≅End_R(E). For complete R it identifies R with End_R(E).
items.note: Refines the existing R03.3 Matlis supplier in PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23/matlis and PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23/matlis. Those proposals are not pinned implementation. Artinian endomorphism and completion-action fine suppliers remain G7.

items.name: Matlis dual detects a nonzero arbitrary module
items.statement: For Noetherian local R and E=E_R(k), every nonzero R-module M has Hom_R(M,E)≠0, without finite generation of M.
items.locator: Hochster Local cohomology (2011), paragraph after Theorem 5.1, p.19

items.name: Top local cohomology commutes with arbitrary tensor coefficients
items.statement: Let R be Noetherian, I=(x_1,…,x_d), and M any R-module. Then H_I^d(M)≅H_I^d(R)⊗_R M, naturally in M. No finite-generation assumption on M is needed.
items.note: The Ext-to-Čech comparison is not in the pinned file: its future-work list says so. Import the single generic Koszul construction from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1; prove the Noetherian local-cohomology comparison in R03.3. No arbitrary non-Noetherian Čech claim.

items.name: Top local cohomology of a regular local ring
items.statement: For a regular Noetherian local ring R of dimension d, H_m^d(R) is an injective envelope of its residue field and is nonzero.
items.note: Use the existing R03.3 regular/CM substrate. The Gorenstein quotient and envelope-union fine decomposition remain G7; the stated regular specialization is not a new generic Gorenstein roadmap.

items.name: Correct duality direction for an arbitrary module
items.statement: For a Noetherian regular local ring R of dimension d, E=E_R(k), and any R-module M, Hom_R(H_m^d(M),E)≅Hom_R(M,Rhat). If R is complete the right side is Hom_R(M,R). Consequently H_m^d(M)≠0 iff Hom_R(M,Rhat)≠0.
items.locator: Repair of André A.3.1 p.91 and Hochster 1983 p.541; follows from Hochster Local cohomology (2011), 5.1, 11.5–11.6

items.name: A pure extension of a complete Noetherian local base splits
items.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring and S a commutative R-algebra. If R→S is pure, there is an R-linear map ρ:S→R with ρ(1)=1. Neither regularity, integrality, finite generation of S nor an endomorphism of S is required.
items.locator: Corrected complete-base branch of André A.3.1; direct proof from Hochster Local cohomology (2011), Theorem 5.1

items.name: Absolute integral closure carrier
items.statement: For a domain R with fraction field K and a chosen algebraic closure Kbar, let R+=integralClosure R Kbar. Its elements are precisely the elements of Kbar integral over R.
items.locator: André §0.2 p.73 and A.3 Applications p.91; Hochster 1983 Theorem 6.1
items.note: Only the underlying integralClosure carrier is library status. Chosen-closure transport and finite-subalgebra APIs need adapters; no canonical choice of every field embedding is asserted.

api.name: mem_integralClosure_iff
api.statement: Membership is IsIntegral R.

api.name: AbsoluteIntegralClosure.finiteSubalgebra
api.statement: A finite set of integral elements is contained in a module-finite R-subalgebra; adapter below.

api.name: AbsoluteIntegralClosure.changeClosure
api.statement: A K-isomorphism of chosen algebraic closures restricts to an R-algebra isomorphism of the integral closures.

uses.how: Use integralClosure with the chosen fraction-field/algebraic-closure towers; avoid a second normal-closure object.

items.name: Integral algebras are filtered unions of finite subalgebras
items.statement: An integral R-algebra S is the filtered union of its module-finite R-subalgebras. If R→S is injective and pure, each inclusion R→S_α in this union is pure. Conversely purity of every R→S_α implies purity of R→S.
items.note: This is the source-specific assembly adapter, not an absence claim for elementary finite-integral-generation lemmas. Fine supplier audit remains G7.

items.name: Pure integral extensions preserve a nonzero top local-cohomology class
items.statement: For regular Noetherian local R of dimension d and an integral pure extension R→S, the map H_m^d(R)→H_m^d(S) is injective, hence the target is nonzero.
items.note: Filtered-colimit comparison must be established for the existing localCohomology functor; no arbitrary inverse-limit/Matlis interchange is used.

items.name: Splitting the absolute integral closure over a complete regular base
items.statement: If R is complete Noetherian regular local and every finite integral extension domain of R splits R-linearly, then R→R+ splits R-linearly. In particular this applies to R=W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]] after Theorem 0.2.1.
items.locator: André §0.2 p.73 and A.3 Applications p.91, with complete-base qualification
items.note: This conditional theorem does not depend on the general direct-summand theorem and so can be used inside its reduction. The printed application to an arbitrary, possibly noncomplete DVR V is not certified by this argument.

items.name: Local and faithfully flat tests for a finite algebra splitting
items.statement: For a Noetherian ring R and finite R-algebra S, R→S splits iff the image of ev_1:Hom_R(S,R)→R is R. This is equivalent to splitting after localization at every maximal ideal. If R→R′ is faithfully flat and R′→R′⊗_R S splits, then R→S splits.

items.name: Canonical-element property in the Koszul formulation
items.statement: A Noetherian local ring (R,m,k) of dimension d has CE if, for every system of parameters x and every projective resolution P_•→k, every chain map K_•(x;R)→P_• lifting R/(x)→k has nonzero component in degree d.
items.locator: Hochster 1983 Definition 2.1 and Remarks 2.2, pp.504–506; used by 6.1
items.note: Generic finite Koszul complexes are imported from DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1, not replanned here. The CE predicate and its source-specific arguments belong to DirectSummandsAndBigCohenMacaulay. No pinned CE declaration found.

api.name: CanonicalElementProperty.resolution_independent
api.statement: Comparison maps show it suffices to use one projective resolution.

api.name: CanonicalElementProperty.parameters_cofinal
api.statement: Testing all positive powers of one parameter system suffices.

api.name: CanonicalElementProperty.descent
api.statement: Descend CE along a local map carrying a parameter system to a parameter system, as in 2.4.

uses.how: Records the intermediary hidden by the phrase reduce to unramified; imports the generic Koszul complex.

items.name: Root-extension splitting criterion for CE
items.statement: Let B be a complete mixed-characteristic local domain, finite over A=V[[x_2,…,x_d]], with V a complete DVR and x_1 its uniformizer. In a fixed algebraic closure choose B∞ integral over B, containing compatible p-power roots x_ie, such that B∞/(x_1^(1/p∞)) is perfect and x_1,x_i are regular for i≥2. If each A_e=A[x_1e,…,x_de] splits in every finite intermediate A_e-algebra inside B∞, then B has CE.
items.note: Source theorem and proof read; the root-ideal complex, distributivity and homotopy lemmas 2.10–2.17 still require individual extraction/API closure, retained in G3. This one theorem is not represented as that finished decomposition.

items.name: CE implies the monomial noncontainment
items.statement: If a d-dimensional Noetherian local ring has CE, x_1,…,x_d is a system of parameters, and t≥1, then (x_1⋯x_d)^(t−1)∉(x_1^t,…,x_d^t).

items.name: Monomial criterion for splitting a finite extension
items.statement: Let A be a regular Noetherian local ring with a regular system of parameters x_1,…,x_d and let A⊂B be finite. Then A→B splits iff (x_1⋯x_d)^(t−1)∉(x_1^t,…,x_d^t)B for every t≥1.
items.note: Exact criterion read in the 1983 source. Reverse implication depends on the Artinian Gorenstein socle/injective-envelope argument of the 1973 source; its fine decomposition remains G3, not inferred just from the existing Artinian inverse-limit item.

items.name: Transport nonvanishing across a finite coefficient DVR extension
items.statement: Let V_0⊂V be a finite extension of complete DVRs, A=V_0[[x_2,…,x_d]], B=V[[x_2,…,x_d]]. In a common algebraic closure of their fraction fields, A+=B+. If H_mA^d(A+)≠0 then H_mB^d(B+)≠0.
items.note: The pinned radical comparison alone does not change the base ring. That additional adapter and the Cohen coefficient theorem producing V_0 remain G3/G7. The source has complete V; no finite-extension assertion for an arbitrary noncomplete DVR is made.

items.name: Extending the contracting power-series endomorphism
items.statement: Let A=V[[x_2,…,x_d]] with V a complete DVR and q≥2. The continuous V-endomorphism σ(x_i)=x_i^q extends to an automorphism of A+. A is finite free over σ(A), with monomial basis whose exponents are <q, and ∩_j σ^j(m_A)A=πA.
items.locator: Hochster 1983 6.1(4°⇒3°), p.541; André A.3 Applications p.91

items.name: A nonzero dual splits the absolute integral closure of a complete DVR power-series ring
items.statement: For A=V[[x_2,…,x_d]] with V a complete DVR, Hom_A(A+,A)≠0 implies that A→A+ splits A-linearly.

items.name: Hochster reduction to complete unramified regular local rings
items.statement: Assume that for every prime p, every complete unramified mixed-characteristic regular local ring A with algebraically closed residue field, and every finite extension domain B of A, the inclusion A→B splits. Then every finite extension of every Noetherian regular ring splits. Thus André’s theorem for W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]] with perfect k suffices.
items.note: The cited theorem and proof are now read. This records the actual reduction, not a claim that its full library/prerequisite decomposition is closed: G3 enumerates remaining coefficient, root-complex and socle adapters. In particular fixed-dimension reduction is not used to deduce a different dimension. The extraction of André's paper records this reduction as the cited theorem it uses. Splitting Hochster's own proof (2.10–2.17, the 1973 socle criterion, coefficient enlargement) is the extraction of Hochster 1983 itself, listed under prerequisites.

items.name: Maximal secant sequence (system of parameters)
items.statement: In a Noetherian local ring R of Krull dimension d, a maximal secant sequence — a “système de paramètres” — is a system (x_1,…,x_d) of d generators of an ideal whose radical is the maximal ideal.
items.locator: §0.1, footnote 1, p.72; used in Definition 4.1.1, p.84
items.note: Searched the pinned trees for IsSystemOfParameters/systemOfParameters/parameterIdeal: absent at the pin. Build it from the pinned Ideal.radical, IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal and ringKrullDim rather than from a private dimension notion; the existing regular-sequence carriers are the consumers.

api.name: IsSecantSequence
api.statement: A list of length ringKrullDim R generating an ideal whose radical is IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R.

api.name: IsSecantSequence.radical_span
api.statement: Expose Ideal.radical (Ideal.span {x_1,…,x_d}) = maximalIdeal R.

api.name: IsSecantSequence.length
api.statement: Expose that the length is the Krull dimension.

uses: Definition 4.1.1 and Theorem 0.7.1, where a maximal secant sequence must become regular in the Cohen–Macaulay algebra; statement (4) of §0.1.

items.name: Rank of a module of finite projective dimension
items.statement: For a finitely generated module of finite projective dimension over a Noetherian local ring, the rank is the alternating sum of the ranks of the free modules in a finite free resolution; it is independent of the resolution.
items.note: Mathlib has ModuleCat.projectiveDimension and TauCeti has ExactStructure.FiniteResolution.syzygy at the pin, but no alternating-rank invariant; independence of the resolution is part of the statement.

api.name: Module.rankOfFiniteProjectiveDimension
api.statement: Alternating sum of the ranks of a finite free resolution.

api.name: Module.rank_independent_of_resolution
api.statement: Two finite free resolutions give the same alternating sum.

uses: Statement (6) of §0.1, where a non-free k-th syzygy of finite projective dimension is asserted to have rank at least k.

items.name: Ideals of a regular ring are contracted from integral extensions
items.statement: For every ideal I of a regular ring R and every integral extension S of R one has I = R ∩ IS. This is statement (2) of §0.1 and is equivalent to the direct summand conjecture.
items.note: One direction is elementary, as the footnote says: purity of S gives injectivity of R/I → S/IS. The converse is the cited Dobbs reference.

items.name: Integral extensions descend flatness
items.statement: Every integral extension of a Noetherian ring descends flatness of modules. This is statement (3) of §0.1, listed there as equivalent to the direct summand conjecture.
items.note: New in the published version; the 2016 preprint's list does not contain it. The printed footnote gives only (1)⇒(3); see source issue E13.

items.name: Monomial conjecture
items.statement: For every Noetherian local ring R, every maximal secant sequence (x_1,…,x_d) and every pair (m,n) ∈ N², the monomial (x_1⋯x_d)^m lies in the ideal generated by x_1^n,…,x_d^n if and only if m ≥ n. This is statement (4) of §0.1 and is equivalent to the direct summand conjecture.
items.note: The “only if” half is the substance; “if” is immediate. The footnote attributes the equivalence (1)⇔(4) to Hochster 1983.

items.name: Dimension bound for a complex with finite-length higher homology
items.statement: For every Noetherian local ring R with maximal ideal m and every complex of finitely generated free modules 0→F_d→⋯→F_0→0 such that H_i(F_•) has finite length for i>0 and some element of H_0(F_•) outside mH_0(F_•) has m-primary torsion, one has dim R ≤ d. This is statement (5) of §0.1.
items.note: The printed footnote gives (4)⇒(5) only, although (5) is listed among the equivalent statements; see source issue E13.

items.name: Syzygy conjecture
items.statement: Every k-th syzygy module of a finitely generated module over a Noetherian local ring that has finite projective dimension and is not free has rank at least k. This is statement (6) of §0.1; it is implied by (1)–(5).

items.name: Equivalence of the homological reformulations
items.statement: Statements (1)–(5) of §0.1 — the direct summand conjecture for every regular ring, contraction of ideals from integral extensions, descent of flatness along integral extensions, the monomial conjecture, and the dimension bound for complexes with finite-length higher homology — are equivalent, and they imply the syzygy conjecture (6).
items.note: Recorded as the paper states it. The printed arrows do not close the equivalence for (3) and (5); the attributions are in the cited literature, not in this paper. See source issue E13.

items.name: Divided trace in invertible degree
items.statement: If R ↪ S is a finite extension whose degree is invertible in R — in particular whenever R contains Q — then a divided trace is an R-linear retraction, so the direct summand conjecture holds for R.
items.note: Stating this needs the reduction that makes the trace available: generic freeness of S over R, then the trace form of the corresponding finite free extension. The pinned Algebra.trace carries the trace itself.

items.name: A finite flat extension splits
items.statement: A finite flat extension R ↪ S of Noetherian rings is faithfully flat, and the exact sequence 0→R→S→S/R→0 splits, because S/R is then finitely presented and flat, hence projective.
items.note: The printed sentence asserts the splitting without naming the projectivity step; the finitely presented flat ⇒ projective input is what makes it work.

items.name: The conjecture in dimension at most two
items.statement: The direct summand conjecture holds for a regular ring of dimension at most 2, because every finite normal extension of such a ring is flat.
items.note: The flatness step is the Auslander–Buchsbaum depth computation; the paper cites it implicitly.

items.name: Heitmann's theorem in dimension three
items.statement: The direct summand conjecture holds for regular local rings of dimension 3 of mixed characteristic (Heitmann).
items.locator: §0.2, p.72, citing Heitmann, The direct summand conjecture in dimension three, Ann. Math. 156 (2002), 695–712
items.note: Cited, not reproved. Recorded as a prerequisite theorem of the subject, not as an input to the proof given here.

items.name: Regularity is necessary
items.statement: In R = K[x,y]/(xy) the ideal (x+y) is not the contraction of any ideal of the normalisation K[x] × K[y]; so the direct summand conjecture fails without regularity, and normality of R would not suffice either.

items.name: Hochster's theorem in characteristic p
items.statement: For a regular Noetherian ring of characteristic p > 0 every module-finite injective extension splits: reduce to a complete local ring with perfect residue field and apply the contracting-endomorphism criterion with r = 0 and σ the Frobenius, which is flat because R is regular and finite in that case.
items.note: Uses the corrected criterion of E4, with r = 0, not the printed form. The reduction to the complete perfect-residue-field case is a separate step recorded under G3.

items.name: Uniform Banach algebra
items.statement: Let 𝒦 be a field complete for a non-trivial valuation. A 𝒦-Banach algebra ℬ is uniform when its norm is equivalent to the associated spectral norm; ℬ_{≤1} denotes its unit ball and ℬ° its subring of power-bounded elements, with ℬ_{≤1} ⊆ ℬ° and equality when ℬ is spectral.
items.locator: §1.2, p.76; the power-bounded comparison is recalled in the proof of Theorem 2.5.2, p.79
items.note: Mathlib has spectralValue/spectralNorm and IsPowMul at the pin, and TauCeti has Huber rings and IsTateRing, but no uniform-Banach predicate; searched both pinned trees for uniform/spectral Banach carriers.

api.name: IsUniformBanachAlgebra
api.statement: A complete normed 𝒦-algebra whose norm is equivalent to its spectral norm.

api.name: IsUniformBanachAlgebra.unitBall
api.statement: Expose ℬ_{≤1} and its comparison with the power-bounded subring ℬ°.

api.name: IsUniformBanachAlgebra.isPowMul_spectral
api.statement: Relate the predicate to the pinned IsPowMul.

uses: §1.2 and §2.4: the Weierstrass localisation is formed inside a uniform Banach algebra, and the tower algebras A_{∞k} are given the unique norm whose unit ball is the integral closure.

items.name: Weierstrass localisation ℬ{f/λ}
items.statement: For 𝒦 complete and non-trivially valued, λ a nonzero element of 𝒦°, ℬ a uniform 𝒦-Banach algebra and f ∈ ℬ_{≤1}, ℬ{f/λ} is the quotient of ℬ⟨U⟩ by the closure of the ideal generated by λU − f, a Banach algebra for the quotient norm, not necessarily uniform. That ideal is closed, so ℬ{f/λ} = ℬ⟨U⟩/(λU − f) — formula (1).
items.note: Closedness is the cited Mihara result, not proved here; it is what turns the quotient by a closure into a quotient by an ideal.

api.name: UniformBanach.weierstrass
api.statement: ℬ⟨U⟩/(λU − f) with its quotient norm.

api.name: UniformBanach.weierstrass_eq_quotient
api.statement: Formula (1): the ideal generated by λU − f is closed, so no closure is needed.

api.name: UniformBanach.weierstrass_universal
api.statement: Maps out of ℬ{f/λ} are maps out of ℬ sending f/λ into the unit ball.

uses: Lemma 2.5.1 and the proof of Theorem 2.5.2, where the tubular neighbourhoods of T = g are the Weierstrass localisations ℬ{(T−g)/π^i}.

items.name: λU − f is a non-zero-divisor
items.statement: If f is a non-zero-divisor in ℬ then λU − f is a non-zero-divisor in ℬ⟨U⟩.

items.name: The unit ball carries the π-adic topology
items.statement: If |𝒦| is dense in |ℬ| — which holds whenever the valuation is non-discrete — then for every π ∈ 𝒦°° the topology of ℬ_{≤1} is the π-adic topology.
items.note: Cited from the companion paper's sorite 2.3.1; it is what lets every later completion be read p-adically or π-adically.

items.name: Unit ball of a Weierstrass localisation, discrete and dense cases
items.statement: Assume |𝒦| dense in |ℬ| and multiplication by f isometric in ℬ — as it is when the norm of ℬ is multiplicative and |f| = 1. Then ℬ_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f) has no π-torsion and (λU − f)ℬ_{≤1} = ((λU − f)ℬ)_{≤1}; consequently ℬ{f/λ}_{≤1} = ℬ_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f) when the valuation of 𝒦 is discrete (formula (2)), and ℬ{f/λ}_{≤1} = (ℬ_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f))^a_* otherwise (formula (3)), the almost functor being taken in the base (𝒦°, 𝒦°°), where ℬ^a_* = ∩_{η ∈ 𝒦°°} η^{-1}ℬ.
items.note: The two cases are genuinely different and both are used: §2 works with a dense valuation, so formula (3) with the almost-* functor is the one in force. The torsion-freeness step is recorded as source issue E14.

items.name: Weierstrass unit ball as a completed subring
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, (λU − f)ℬ_{≤1}⟨U⟩ is closed in ℬ_{≤1}⟨U⟩ and ℬ_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f) is π-adically separated and equal to the π-adic completion of ℬ_{≤1}[f/λ] ⊆ ℬ — formula (4). The proof runs through the exactness of 0 → (λU − f)ℬ_{≤1}[U] → ℬ_{≤1}[U] → ℬ_{≤1}[f/λ] → 0 (formula (5)) and of its completion (formula (6)).

items.name: Invariance of the Weierstrass algebra under approximation
items.statement: ℬ_{≤1}⟨U⟩/(λU − f) does not change, up to isomorphism, when f is replaced by f′ with |f − f′| ≤ |λ|, or λ by λ′ with |λ| = |λ′|; the isomorphism is induced by U ↦ (λ/λ′)(U + h) with h = λ^{-1}(f′ − f) ∈ ℬ_{≤1}.
items.note: This is the approximation step used twice in the proof of Theorem 2.5.2, to replace f_i^{1/p^k} and π^{i/p^k} by elements of a finite stage.

items.name: Completely integrally closed subring
items.statement: A subring A of a ring B is completely integrally closed in B when every element of B whose powers lie in a single finitely generated A-submodule of B belongs to A.
items.note: Searched the pinned trees for IsCompletelyIntegrallyClosed: absent. It is strictly stronger than the pinned IsIntegrallyClosed and is what the norm construction of §2.4 needs.

api.name: IsCompletelyIntegrallyClosedIn
api.statement: Every b ∈ B whose powers lie in one finitely generated A-submodule of B lies in A.

api.name: IsCompletelyIntegrallyClosedIn.isIntegrallyClosedIn
api.statement: The condition implies the pinned integral closedness.

api.name: IsCompletelyIntegrallyClosedIn.of_directed_union
api.statement: A directed union of Noetherian integrally closed subrings, finite over one another, is completely integrally closed in the corresponding union.

uses: §2.3 for A°_{∞k} inside A_{∞k}, which is what §2.4 needs to produce the spectral norm; ordinary integral closedness would not suffice.

items.name: Integral closures in the normalized Kummer tower
items.statement: A°_{jk} contains K°_j[[T^{1/p^j}_{≤n}]][g^{1/p^k}] and satisfies A_{jk} = A°_{jk}[1/p]. For (j,k) ∈ N² it is Noetherian and p-adically complete. For j = ∞ it is the increasing union of the A°_{j′k′}, which are Noetherian, integrally closed in A_{j′k′} and finite over one another, so A°_{∞k} is completely integrally closed in A_{∞k}. Moreover A°_{j′k′} = A°_{jk} ∩ A_{j′k′} for j′ ≤ j, k′ ≤ k, and A°_{00} = A.
items.note: Complete integral closedness for j = ∞, not mere integral closedness, is the hypothesis of the norm statement in §2.4; the union is not Noetherian.

items.name: Unique norm with a completely integrally closed unit ball
items.statement: Since A°_{∞k} is completely integrally closed in A_{∞k} and |K_∞| is dense in R_+, there is a unique K_∞-algebra norm on A_{∞k} whose unit ball is A°_{∞k}, and this norm is spectral, that is power-multiplicative.
items.locator: §2.4, p.79, citing the companion paper's sorite 2.3.1(4)
items.note: The companion PAPER-ANDRE-18 owns the generic sorite; this paper is its consumer. Mathlib's IsPowMul is the power-multiplicativity carrier at the pin.

items.name: Unit balls and isometric transition maps
items.statement: For the induced spectral norm on A_{jk} the unit ball is A°_{jk}, and as (j,k) varies the transition maps of the system (A°_{jk}) — the natural inclusions — are isometric. The A_{j0} are multiplicatively normed; this need not hold for A_{jk} when k ≠ 0.

items.name: The ideal of topologically nilpotent elements of the coordinate tower
items.statement: The ideal A°°_{∞0} of topologically nilpotent elements of A°_{∞0} is an idempotent prime ideal, equal to K°°_∞ A°_{∞0}.
items.note: This identification is what lets the proof of Theorem 2.5.2 move between the almost bases (K°_∞, K°°_∞) and (A°_{∞0}, A°°_{∞0}). TauCeti has IsTopologicallyNilpotent and Huber pseudouniformizers at the pin; idempotence of this particular ideal is specific.

items.name: Normality of the Kummer algebras
items.statement: If g is square-free in the factorial ring A[1/p] and is not divisible by any of the T_h, then all the A_{jk} and A°_{jk} are normal.

items.name: A domain criterion by Capelli–Vahlen
items.statement: If ±g is not the product of a monomial in the T_h and a p-th power in A, then A_{jk} is a domain; the proof uses the Capelli–Vahlen irreducibility criterion for X^{p^k} − g.
items.note: Needed because the construction adjoins a root of X^{p^k} − g: without such a hypothesis A_{jk} need not be a domain, as the paper warns in the note to the tower construction.

items.name: Multiplicativity of the norm of a Kummer algebra
items.statement: If ±g mod p is not the product of a monomial in the T_h and a p-th power in A/p, then the norm of A_{jk} is multiplicative.

items.name: Ramifying several elements at once
items.statement: The construction and Theorem 2.5.2 extend from a single g to finitely many elements g^{(1)},…,g^{(m)} of A, by introducing indeterminates T^{(1)},…,T^{(m)} in place of the single T.

api.name: NormalizedKummerTower.multi
api.statement: The tower attached to a finite family (g^{(1)},…,g^{(m)}) with indeterminates T^{(1)},…,T^{(m)}.

api.name: NormalizedKummerTower.multi_eq_single
api.statement: For m = 1 it is the tower of §2.2.

api.name: NormalizedKummerTower.multi_almostFlat
api.statement: Theorem 2.5.2 holds for the multi-element tower.

uses: Remark 2.6.1(4), and through it the §4.4 discussion where more than one discriminant has to be ramified at once.

items.name: A possibly ramified regular base
items.statement: A may be replaced by a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0,p) with perfect residue field that is possibly ramified, even though there is then no perfectoid base field.
items.note: This variant is what §4.4 uses to drop the unramifiedness of A′ in the weak functoriality discussion.

items.name: Only the statement modulo powers of p is needed
items.statement: In the applications only the reduction of Theorem 2.5.2 modulo each power of p is used, which dispenses with the subtleties about completions and with the final reduction to the Noetherian case.
items.note: Recorded because §§3.3 and 4.4 rely on it explicitly; it narrows what a formalisation of 2.5.2 must deliver for the main theorems.

items.name: Finitely presented modules commute with arbitrary products
items.statement: For a finitely presented R-module P and an arbitrary family (M_i)_{i∈I} of R-modules, the canonical map P ⊗_R ∏_{i∈I} M_i → ∏_{i∈I} (P ⊗_R M_i) is an isomorphism.
items.locator: Lemma A.2.1(1), p.90 — the step on which product stability rests
items.note: At the pin TensorProduct.piRight is proved only for a finite index type: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/Pi.lean states “In general, this is not an isomorphism, but if ι is finite, then it is”. The arbitrary-index statement for finitely presented P is missing and must be proved from a finite presentation.

items.name: Products of pure monomorphisms over a fixed base
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and I an arbitrary index set. If M_i ⊆ N_i is a pure R-submodule for every i ∈ I, then ∏_{i∈I} M_i ⊆ ∏_{i∈I} N_i is pure. In particular, if R ↪ S_i is a pure R-algebra map for every i, then the induced R → ∏_{i∈I} S_i is pure.
items.note: The index set is arbitrary and the base R is fixed: this is the exact form the lemma needs, and it is what §4.3 uses for the product T = ∏_{m,i} T_{m,i} over the maximal ideals of R.

items.name: Artin–Rees lemma
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring, I an ideal, M a finite R-module and N a submodule. There is k such that for every n ≥ k, I^n M ∩ N = I^(n−k)(I^k M ∩ N).
items.note: Read at the pin: Mathlib/RingTheory/Filtration.lean:388, stated for submodules of a finite module over a Noetherian ring. André uses it to make 0 → M1/I^(n−m)N1 → M2/I^n M2 → M3/I^n M3 → 0 exact.

items.name: Krull intersection theorem
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring, J an ideal and M a finite R-module. An element x ∈ M lies in ⋂_n J^n M if and only if (1 − r)x = 0 for some r ∈ J. In particular ⋂_n J^n = 0 when R is local and J is proper.
items.locator: Lemma 1.1.2 proof, p.76; Lemma A.2.2 proof, p.90
items.note: Read at the pin: Mathlib/RingTheory/Filtration.lean:392 (the r • x = x form, which is the (1 − r)x = 0 form André uses) and :431 (the local case).

items.name: Nakayama's lemma
items.statement: Let R be a ring, I an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical and N a finitely generated R-module. If N ⊆ I N then N = 0.
items.locator: Lemma 1.1.1 proof, p.76; Proposition A.3.1 proof, p.91
items.note: Read at the pin: Mathlib/RingTheory/Nakayama.lean:118 (Submodule form N ≤ I • N ⇒ N = ⊥ for I ≤ jacobson ⊥).

items.name: Faithful flatness by proper ideals
items.statement: An R-module M is faithfully flat if and only if it is flat and I M ≠ M for every proper ideal I of R. For a local ring R it suffices that M be flat and m_R M ≠ M.
items.note: Read at the pin: Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/FaithfullyFlat/Basic.lean:73. The local form follows because every proper ideal lies in m_R.

items.name: Lying over for integral extensions
items.statement: Let R → S be an integral ring map, P a prime of R and I an ideal of S with I ∩ R ⊆ P. There is a prime Q ⊇ I of S with Q ∩ R = P. In particular an injective integral map from a domain has a prime of S over (0).
items.note: Read at the pin: Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/GoingUp.lean:327, namespace Ideal, no domain hypothesis on S.

items.name: Finiteness of the integral closure in a separable extension
items.statement: Let A be an integrally closed Noetherian domain with fraction field K, L a finite separable extension of K and C the integral closure of A in L. Then C is a finite A-module.
items.locator: §3.1, p.83 (passage to a Galois extension); used through galois-closure-reduction
items.note: Read at the pin: Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/IntegralClosure.lean:175. In André's use K has characteristic 0, so separability is automatic.

items.name: Reduction modulo p^m stays injective
items.statement: Let A be a domain with p ≠ 0 in A that is integrally closed in A[1/p], and let A → B be an injective integral ring map. Then p^m B ∩ A = p^m A for every m ∈ N; equivalently A/p^m A → B/p^m B is injective.
items.locator: §3.1, p.83 (“Comme A est intégralement fermé dans A[1/p], A/p^m → B/p^m est injectif”)
items.note: Proof: if a = p^m b with b ∈ B, the monic equation of b over A, read in B[1/p], is satisfied by a/p^m ∈ A[1/p]; since A[1/p] → B[1/p] is injective the equation holds in A[1/p], so a/p^m is integral over A and lies in A. A = W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]] is a regular local ring, hence normal.

items.name: Reduction of the direct summand problem to a finite domain extension
items.statement: Let A be a domain and A → B an injective finite ring map. There is a prime P of B with P ∩ A = 0, so A → B/P is an injective finite map to a domain, and if A → B/P is pure (respectively split) then so is A → B. When A has characteristic 0, B/P is p-torsion-free and reduced.
items.locator: §3.1, p.83 (“on peut supposer B réduit et sans p-torsion (on peut en fait supposer B intègre [13, lemma 3])”)
items.note: The retraction of A → B/P composed with B → B/P is a retraction of A → B; for purity use pure-left-factor. This is the form of Hochster 1973 Lemma 3 André cites; the stronger reduced/p-torsion-free normalisation is a consequence.

items.name: Passing to a Galois extension
items.statement: Let A = W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]] and let A → B be a finite injective map to a domain. Let L be a finite Galois extension of Frac(A) containing Frac(B) and B′ the integral closure of A in L. Then B′ is a finite A-algebra containing B, and if A → B′ is pure (respectively split) then so is A → B. After inverting a suitable g ∈ A ∖ pA, B′[1/(pg)] is a finite étale Galois extension of A[1/(pg)].
items.locator: §3.1, p.83 (“et même que B[1/(pg)] soit une extension galoisienne de A[1/(pg)]”)
items.note: Finiteness of B′ uses integral-closure-finite (Frac(A) has characteristic 0). Footnote 4 of §3.2 says the Galois case of the perfectoid Abhyankar lemma suffices; this item is why.

items.name: Choice of the discriminant g
items.statement: Let A = W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]] and let A → B be finite and injective with B reduced and p-torsion-free. There is g ∈ A ∖ pA such that B[1/(pg)] is finite étale over A[1/(pg)].
items.locator: §3.1, p.83 (“Prenons g ∈ A ∖ pA de sorte que B[1/(pg)] soit étale sur A[1/(pg)]”)
items.note: Frac(A) ⊗_A B is a finite reduced algebra over a field of characteristic 0, hence étale; étaleness spreads out to B[1/h] over A[1/h] for some h ≠ 0. Write h = p^a g with g ∉ pA (possible since ⋂ p^a A = 0 by krull-intersection); then A[1/(ph)] = A[1/(pg)].

items.name: Partial algebra modification of degree n
items.statement: Let (B, m_B) be a Noetherian local ring with a system of parameters x = (x_1,…,x_d), M a B-module, 0 ≤ i < d, and m_1,…,m_(i+1) ∈ M with x_(i+1) m_(i+1) = Σ_(j≤i) x_j m_j. For an integer n ≥ 1 put F = m_(i+1) − Σ_(j≤i) x_j T_j ∈ M[T_1,…,T_i] = M ⊗_B B[T_1,…,T_i] and M′ = M[T_1,…,T_i]_(≤n) / F · B[T_1,…,T_i]_(≤n−1), where the subscript bounds the total degree and F is multiplied by polynomials with coefficients in B. The partial modification of degree n of M relative to (B, x) is the B-linear map M → M′ sending m to the constant polynomial m. In M′ the element m_(i+1) lies in (x_1,…,x_i)M′.
items.locator: §4.1, p.85; Hochster 2002 §§3–4 as recalled in Heitmann–Ma, arXiv:1703.08281v2 §1.2
items.note: Corrected statement (E16): the printed text multiplies F by M[T_1,…,T_i]_(≤n−1), a product of two module-valued polynomials that is not defined; the multiplier ring is B[T_1,…,T_i]_(≤n−1). Hochster 2002 itself could not be downloaded (ScienceDirect returns 403); the definition follows Heitmann–Ma, who state that theirs is Hochster's.

api.name: PartialModification.carrier
api.statement: M′ as the quotient of M ⊗_B B[T_1,…,T_i]_(≤n) by the B-submodule F · B[T_1,…,T_i]_(≤n−1), for a relation x_(i+1)m_(i+1) = Σ_(j≤i) x_j m_j and degree bound n.

api.name: PartialModification.map
api.statement: The B-linear map M → M′ sending m to the constant polynomial m.

api.name: PartialModification.trivializes
api.statement: The image of m_(i+1) lies in (x_1,…,x_i)M′.

api.name: PartialModification.degreeMap
api.statement: For n ≤ n′ the inclusion of degree-bounded polynomials induces M′_n → M′_(n′) compatible with the maps from M.

uses.how: The step of Hochster's modification technique whose denominators hochster-key-lemma controls.

items.name: Sequences of partial modifications and the modification algebra
items.statement: Fix (B, x) as in partial-modification. A finite sequence of partial modifications of degree ≤ n relative to (B, x) is B = M_1 → M_2 → ⋯ → M_ℓ with each M_(t+1) a partial modification of M_t. It is bad if the image of 1 ∈ B in M_ℓ lies in m_B M_ℓ. The filtered colimit of all such sequences, over all n and ℓ, carries a B-algebra structure C_x(B) in which x is a possibly improper regular sequence, and m_B C_x(B) ≠ C_x(B) if and only if no finite sequence is bad.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.1.2, p.85 (“Lorsque (n, ℓ, M) varie, la colimite (filtrante) des M_ℓ …”); Heitmann–Ma §1.2 and Theorem 1.6
items.note: The algebra structure is Hochster's algebra modification; the partial (degree-bounded) modifications compute its underlying module as a filtered colimit.

api.name: ModificationSequence
api.statement: A finite chain B = M_1 → ⋯ → M_ℓ of partial modifications relative to (B, x), with degree bound n.

api.name: ModificationSequence.IsBad
api.statement: The image of 1 ∈ B in M_ℓ lies in m_B M_ℓ.

api.name: modificationAlgebra
api.statement: The filtered colimit over all sequences, with its B-algebra structure (Hochster's algebra modification), in which x is a possibly improper regular sequence.

uses.how: Carries the no-bad-sequence criterion from almost Cohen–Macaulay data to a Cohen–Macaulay algebra.

items.name: Hochster's criterion for a Cohen–Macaulay algebra for (B, x)
items.statement: Let (B, m_B) be a Noetherian local ring with system of parameters x. There is a B-algebra C with m_B C ≠ C in which x is a regular sequence if and only if no finite sequence of partial modifications of B relative to (B, x) is bad; in that case C_x(B) is such an algebra.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.1.2, p.85; Hochster 2002 Theorem 4.2 as recalled in Heitmann–Ma Theorem 1.6 (case R = S)
items.note: Only the direction ‘no bad sequence ⇒ C_x(B) is Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x)’ is used by André.

items.name: Hochster's denominator lemma
items.statement: Let B, x be as above, M a B-module, T a B-algebra, c ∈ T a non-zero-divisor and α: M → T[1/c] a B-linear map with α(M) ⊆ c^(−N)T. Suppose that for every i < d, x_(i+1) t_(i+1) = Σ_(j≤i) x_j t_j with t_j ∈ T implies c t_(i+1) ∈ (x_1,…,x_i)T. Then for every partial modification M → M′ of degree ≤ D relative to (B, x), α extends to a B-linear map β: M′ → T[1/c] with β(M′) ⊆ c^(−N′)T, where N′ depends only on N and D.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 4.1.2, p.85 (“Le lemme crucial [15, 5.1] (où l'on prend c = π^(1/p^m) pour m arbitraire)”); Heitmann–Ma Lemma 3.5
items.note: Heitmann–Ma state the lemma with N′ = ND + N + D, in a variant where p is adjoined as an extra parameter; the form above, without that extra parameter, is the one André applies. The original Hochster 2002 Lemma 5.1 was not accessible; the reviewer should compare the hypotheses with it.

items.name: An almost Cohen–Macaulay algebra excludes bad sequences
items.statement: If D is almost Cohen–Macaulay for (B, x, π^(1/p^∞)), then no finite sequence of partial modifications of B relative to (B, x) is bad. More precisely, for every sequence B = M_1 → ⋯ → M_ℓ of degree ≤ n and every h there is m such that B → D extends to maps M_t → π^(−1/p^h)D compatible along the sequence, so the image of 1 in M_ℓ is not in m_B M_ℓ.
