items.note: Apply hochster-key-lemma with T = D and c = π^(1/p^m); the colon ideals of D are killed by every c. After ℓ steps the image lies in c^(−N_ℓ)D with N_ℓ depending only on n and ℓ, and one chooses m with N_ℓ/p^m ≤ 1/p^h. If 1 were in m_B M_ℓ then π^(1/p^h) ∈ m_B D for every h, contradicting almost Cohen–Macaulayness. See E18 and E19 for the printed wording.

items.name: Completion makes a Cohen–Macaulay algebra balanced
items.statement: Let (B, m_B) be a Noetherian local ring and C a B-algebra with m_B C ≠ C in which one system of parameters x is a regular sequence. Then the m_B-adic completion of C is a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra: every system of parameters of B is a regular sequence on it and it is not equal to m_B times itself.
items.locator: §4.1, p.85 (“On « passe » de (1) à (2) en complétant C m_B-adiquement [2, th. 1.7]”)
items.note: Bartijn–Strooker, Modifications monomiales (LNM 1029, 1983), Theorem 1.7, not read (paywalled); Heitmann–Ma §1.2 invoke the same fact as Bruns–Herzog Corollary 8.5.3. The printed title of [2] is wrong (E22).

items.name: Reductions for the existence of big Cohen–Macaulay algebras
items.statement: Let (B, m_B) be a Noetherian local ring. (1) If P is a minimal prime with dim B/P = dim B, a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B/P-algebra is one for B. (2) A balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for the completion B̂ is one for B. (3) If B is complete and p-torsion-free of residue characteristic p, B_red is p-torsion-free and a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B_red-algebra is one for B. (4) If B is complete with residue field k and coefficient ring Λ, then B̂⊗_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞)) is a complete Noetherian local ring faithfully flat over B, and a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra for it is one for B.
items.locator: §4.2, p.86 (“On peut compléter, puis quotienter par le nilradical … remplacer B par l'extension (fidèlement plate) B⊗̂_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞))”) and §0.7, p.75
items.note: In each case a system of parameters of B maps to one of the new ring. (1) reduces the general case to a complete local domain, either containing a field (Hochster, known) or of characteristic (0, p) and p-torsion-free, which is the meaning of ‘d'inégale caractéristique (0,p) (sans p-torsion)’ in §0.7. (3): if px is nilpotent and p is a non-zero-divisor then x is nilpotent.

items.name: Presenting B as a finite extension of an unramified power series ring
items.statement: Let B be a complete Noetherian local ring, reduced and p-torsion-free, of dimension n+1 with perfect residue field k, and let x = (x_1,…,x_(n+1)) be a system of parameters with x_1 = p^2. Then T_i ↦ x_(i+1) makes B a finite extension (injective and module-finite) of A = W(k)[[T_1,…,T_n]].
items.locator: §4.2, p.86 (“Le choix d'une suite sécante maximale x de B avec x_1 = p^2 permet d'écrire B comme extension finie de A := Λ[[T_1,…,T_n]]”)
items.note: Uses the Cohen structure theorem for the coefficient ring W(k) and completeness: B/(p, x_2,…,x_(n+1)) has finite length, so B is finite over A; injectivity because dim B = dim A and A is a domain. The pinned libraries have no Cohen structure theorem.

items.name: Normalization of a finite algebra over a complete regular local ring
items.statement: Let R̂ be a complete regular local ring and S′ a finite R̂-algebra. The normalization of S′_red is finite over R̂ and is a finite product of complete local normal domains S_i, each finite over R̂. If R̂ → S′ is injective, at least one S_i receives R̂ injectively.
items.locator: §4.3, p.87 (“R̂_m est un anneau local régulier complet, donc excellent, de sorte que le normalisé de S ⊗_R R̂_m est un produit fini d'anneaux locaux complets intègres S_(m,i) finis sur R̂_m”)
items.note: Finiteness of normalization is the Nagata property of complete local rings; the last sentence is lying over for the injective finite map, and is what corrects E20.

items.name: Products of flat modules over a Noetherian ring
items.statement: Over a Noetherian ring (more generally a coherent ring) every product of flat modules is flat.
items.locator: §4.3, p.87 (“comme R est noethérien, T := ∏ T_(m,i) est encore plat sur R”)
items.note: Chase's theorem. The pinned Mathlib has no coherent-ring predicate.

items.name: Coefficient rings under a separable residue extension
items.statement: Let β: B → B′ be a local homomorphism of complete Noetherian local rings of characteristic (0, p) whose residue field extension k → k′ is separable. For every coefficient ring Λ of B there is a coefficient ring Λ′ of B′ with β(Λ) ⊆ Λ′.
items.locator: §4.4(1), pp.87–88, citing Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, 29.5 and 29.6
items.note: Stated as André uses it; Matsumura was not read. Separability makes a Cohen ring of k′ formally smooth over Λ, which gives the lift.

items.name: Passage to a perfect residue field
items.statement: Let B be a complete Noetherian local ring of characteristic (0, p) with residue field k and coefficient ring Λ. B⊗̂_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞)) is the m_B-adic completion of B ⊗_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞)); it is a complete Noetherian local ring with residue field k^(1/p^∞), faithfully flat over B. Under coefficient-ring-compatibility, β induces a local homomorphism B⊗̂_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞)) → B′⊗̂_(Λ′) W(k′^(1/p^∞)).
items.note: Without separability the extension of scalars is not weakly functorial in (B, k) (§4.4(1)).

api.name: completedCoefficientExtension
api.statement: The m_B-adic completion of B ⊗_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞)) for a chosen coefficient ring Λ ⊆ B.

api.name: completedCoefficientExtension.isLocal
api.statement: It is a complete Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal generated by m_B and residue field k^(1/p^∞).

api.name: completedCoefficientExtension.faithfullyFlat
api.statement: The structure map from B is faithfully flat.

api.name: completedCoefficientExtension.map
api.statement: A local map β with separable residue extension and compatible coefficient rings induces a local map of the extensions.

uses.how: Reduces 0.7.1 and the weak-functoriality problem to perfect residue fields.

items.name: Purity survives completion and passage to perfect residue fields
items.statement: Let B → B′ be a pure local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings of characteristic (0, p) with separable residue field extension. Then B̂ → B̂′ is pure, and with compatible coefficient rings the induced map B̂⊗̂_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞)) → B̂′⊗̂_(Λ′) W(k′^(1/p^∞)) is pure.
items.locator: §4.4, p.88 (“l'hypothèse de pureté se conserve par complétion et passage aux corps résiduels parfaits en vertu du lemme A.2.2”)
items.note: Base change of the pure map along B̂ → B̂⊗_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞)) is pure. Then Λ′⊗_Λ W(k^(1/p^∞)) → W(k′^(1/p^∞)) is, after p-adic completion, a local map of complete discrete valuation rings with uniformizer p (k′ ⊗_k k^(1/p^∞) is a field because k′/k is separable), hence faithfully flat. Compose and complete with pure-local-completion.

items.name: The example Z_p[[T]] → Z_p[[T,U]]/(T^2 − TU + p)
items.statement: Let B = Z_p[[T]] and B′ = Z_p[[T,U]]/(T^2 − TU + p), with β(T) = T. (1) B′ ≅ Z_p[[T,V]]/(TV − p) is a regular local ring of dimension 2. (2) No parameter of B/pB = F_p[[T]] maps to a parameter of B′/pB′ = F_p[[T,U]]/(T(T − U)). (3) Consequently there is no commutative square of local maps A → A′, A → B, A′ → B′ with A and A′ complete unramified regular local rings and A → B, A′ → B′ finite injective.
items.note: (1): put V = U − T. (2): a parameter of F_p[[T]] is T^a·unit with a ≥ 1, and B′/(p, T^a) surjects onto F_p[[U]], which has infinite length. (3): A = A′ = Z_p[[S]] by dimension and residue fields; the image of S in B/p is a parameter, so by (2) its image in B′/p is not; finiteness of A′/p → B′/p then forces α(S) ∈ pA′, whence the image of S in B′/p is 0, while it equals T^a·unit ≠ 0.

items.name: When β(g) vanishes
items.statement: Let A → B be finite with A regular and g ∈ A such that B[1/(pg)] is étale over A[1/(pg)], and let β: B → B′ be a homomorphism to a domain of characteristic 0. If the generic point of Spec B′[1/p] maps into the singular locus of Spec B[1/p], then β(g) = 0. If instead β(g) is a non-zero-divisor in D′, replacing g′ by g′·β(g) makes δ((ϖg)^(1/p^m)) divide (ϖg′)^(1/p^m).
items.note: Points of Spec B[1/(pg)] are étale over the regular A[1/p], hence regular, so the singular locus of Spec B[1/p] lies in V(g); a function vanishing at the generic point of a domain is 0.

items.name: Weak functoriality when the target is regular
items.statement: Let β: B → B′ be an injective local homomorphism of complete Noetherian local domains of characteristic (0, p) with separable residue field extension and B′ regular. There are a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B-algebra C, a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B′-algebra C′ and a ring map γ: C → C′ whose composite with B → C equals the composite of β with B′ → C′.
items.locator: §4.4, p.88 (“le problème de fonctorialité faible a une réponse positive si β est injectif, k → k′ séparable, et B′ régulier”)
items.note: Outline in the paper: after passing to perfect residue fields, take D as in §4.2 for B and D′ := g^(−1/p^∞) Â′_∞⟨ζ_(p^∞), g^(1/p^∞), T_1^(1/p^∞),…,T_n^(1/p^∞)⟩°, with A′ = B′ allowed ramified (Remark 2.6.1(4)); read T_i and g as their images in B′, ramified over B′ by the several-element variant of Remark 2.6.1(4), so that the tower of A maps to D′. D′ is integrally closed in D′[1/(pg)] (companion Lemma 4.2.3), which gives δ: D → D′, and Proposition 4.4.1 finishes. The general statement for every local homomorphism of complete local domains is André, Weak functoriality of Cohen–Macaulay algebras, arXiv:1801.10010v3, Theorem 1.1.1.

items.name: Cohen–Macaulayness descends along a pure map to a regular ring with a compatible square
items.statement: Let B → B′ be a pure local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with B′ regular. Suppose there are a B-algebra C in which a system of parameters x of B is a regular sequence, a balanced big Cohen–Macaulay B′-algebra C′ and a ring map C → C′ compatible with B → B′. Then x is a regular sequence on B, so B is Cohen–Macaulay.
items.locator: §4.4, p.88 (“Par un argument connu (cf. [17, 2.3] …)”), Hochster–Huneke 1995 (2.3), not read
items.note: Proof: C′ is faithfully flat over B′ (regular-big-cm-flat), so B → C′ is pure and ideals of B are contracted from C′. If x_(i+1) b ∈ (x_1,…,x_i)B then b ∈ (x_1,…,x_i)C, hence b ∈ (x_1,…,x_i)C′ ∩ B = (x_1,…,x_i)B.

items.name: Cohen–Macaulayness and completion
items.statement: A Noetherian local ring B is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if its m_B-adic completion is.
items.locator: §4.4, p.88, reduction of Theorem 4.4.2 to complete rings
items.note: Depth and dimension are unchanged by completion. The finite depth/Cohen–Macaulay substrate is planned in R03.3 (finite-cm-substrate); this comparison belongs with it.

items.name: The coordinate tower and its root algebra are perfectoid
items.statement: In the setting of §2.2, Â_∞0 is a perfectoid K̂_∞-algebra, and so is Â_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩, the p-adic completion of A_∞0[T^(1/p^∞)], which is also its completion for the multiplicative Gauss norm. Formula (10): Â_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩° = Â°_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩ = Â_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩_(≤1), and T − g has norm 1.
items.locator: §2.5, formula (10), p.79; proof of Theorem 2.5.2, p.79, citing [1, ex. 3.2.3 (1), (2)]
items.note: Companion Exemples 3.2.3 read in the published version: A⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩ is perfectoid for perfectoid A.

items.name: Â_∞∞ is perfectoid
items.statement: The K̂_∞-algebra Â_∞∞ is perfectoid.
items.locator: §3.1, p.83, citing [1, §3.6.2]; the cited result is [1, §3.6.1] (E17)
items.note: Via Lemma 2.5.1 and the companion's Corollary 2.9.3, Â_∞∞ is the root algebra Â_∞0⟨g^(1/p^∞)⟩, which is perfectoid by the companion's §3.6.1 (an extremal quotient of the perfectoid Â_∞0⊗̂K⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩).

items.name: Approximation by untilts (Scholze)
items.statement: Let (R, R^+) be a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra with tilt (R^♭, R^(♭+)), X = Spa(R, R^+), and ϖ as in Scholze §5 with |p| ≤ |ϖ| < 1. For every f ∈ R, c ≥ 0 and ε > 0 there is g_(c,ε) ∈ R^♭ with |f(x) − g_(c,ε)^♯(x)| ≤ |ϖ|^(1−ε) max(|f(x)|, |ϖ|^c) for all x ∈ X.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.5.2, p.79, citing [22, cor. 6.7 i]; Scholze 2012 Corollary 6.7(i), p.290
items.note: Read in the published Scholze 2012. PerfectoidSpaces:P2 plans the tilting homeomorphism with its rational-subset correspondence, whose proof in Scholze is Corollary 6.7(i)–(iii).

items.name: Replacing T − g by an element with p-power roots
items.statement: For every i ≥ 1 there is f_i ∈ Â°_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩ admitting compatible roots f_i^(1/p^k) in Â°_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩ with f_i ≡ T − g modulo ϖ′ (ϖ′ fixed with |ϖ| < |ϖ′| < 1), such that Â_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩{(T−g)/ϖ^i}° ≅ Â_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩{f_i/ϖ^i}° (formula (11)).
items.note: Apply scholze-approximation to f = T − g with c ≥ i and |ϖ|^(1−ε) ≤ |ϖ′|, and set f_i = g_(c,ε)^♯. Then {|T − g| ≤ |ϖ|^i} and {|f_i| ≤ |ϖ|^i} are the same rational subset, so the localizations agree. The printed ‘congru à T − g modulo ϖ’ is stronger than the citation gives (E23); the proof uses only the congruence modulo ϖ′.

items.name: Unit ball of the tubular neighbourhood as a completed colimit
items.statement: In the almost setting (K°_∞, K°°_∞), Â_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩{(T−g)/ϖ^i}°^a ≅ (ĉolim_k Â°_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞)⟩[(f_i/ϖ^i)^(1/p^k)])^a ≅ ĉolim_k (Â°_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞), U⟩/(ϖ^(i/p^k)U − f_i^(1/p^k)))^a (formula (13)), where ĉolim is the p-adically completed colimit.
items.note: Combine tube-sharp-approximation, perfectoid-rational-integral-model (Scholze Lemma 6.4(ii) with numerators f_i^♭ and ϖ^(♭i), denominator ϖ^(♭i)), the colimit comparison checked modulo ϖ^n, and weierstrass-integral-completion (formula (4)).

items.name: Descent of the tubular algebras to Noetherian stages
items.statement: Fix (i, k). For j large there are f_ik ∈ A°_j0⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩, ϖ_ik ∈ K_j with |ϖ_ik| = |ϖ|^(i/p^k), g_k ∈ A°_j0⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩ with g_k^(p^k) ≡ g modulo ϖ, and a uniformizer ϖ_j of K°_j with |ϖ_j| ≥ |ϖ′|^(1/p^k) > |ϖ_ik| (15), such that: (14) Â°_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞), U⟩/(ϖ^(i/p^k)U − f_i^(1/p^k)) ≅ Â°_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞), U⟩/(ϖ_ik U − f_ik); (16) ĉolim_j A°_j0⟨T^(1/p^j), U⟩/(ϖ_ik U − f_ik) ≅ Â°_∞0⟨T^(1/p^∞), U⟩/(ϖ_ik U − f_ik); (17) A°_j0⟨T^(1/p^j), U⟩/(ϖ_ik U − f_ik) = A_j0⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩{f_ik/ϖ_ik}_(≤1).
items.note: (14) is weierstrass-invariance; (16) is checked modulo ϖ_ik^n; (17) is the discretely valued unit-ball formula (2), valid because A_j0⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩ has multiplicative norm and |f_ik| = 1. The element g_k may be taken in A°_j0: Â_∞0 is perfectoid, and uniqueness of p^k-th roots modulo ϖ^(1/p^k) shows that any choice is T-free modulo ϖ_j. That is what special-fibre-free needs.

items.name: Flatness from the generic and special fibres
items.statement: Let R be a ring, π ∈ R a non-zero-divisor and M an R-module on which π is a non-zero-divisor. If M/πM is flat over R/πR and M[1/π] is flat over R[1/π], then M is flat over R.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.5.2, p.81 (“D'après le critère de platitude par fibres sur A°_j0”)
items.note: Proof: for N killed by π, Tor_i^R(N, M) = Tor_i^(R/π)(N, M/πM) = 0 for i ≥ 1 because π is regular on R and on M; pass to π-power torsion N by filtration and colimits; for π-torsion-free N use N → N[1/π] and flatness of M[1/π]. The π-torsion-freeness of the Noetherian stage holds by (17), a unit ball.

items.name: Flatness of affinoid (Weierstrass) localization
items.statement: For a K-affinoid algebra B and an affinoid domain V ⊆ M(B), the restriction B → B_V is flat. In particular B⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩ → B⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩{f/λ} is flat.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.5.2, p.81, citing [3, prop. 2.2.4] (Berkovich 1990)
items.note: Berkovich 1990 was not read (not public). The Tau Ceti AdicSpaces layer plans flatness of restriction maps between rational localisations for strongly Noetherian Tate rings, which contains this case.

items.name: Flatness of the generic fibre of the Noetherian stage
items.statement: A_j0⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩{f_ik/ϖ_ik} is flat over A_j0 = A°_j0[1/p].
items.note: The analytic spectrum of A_j0 is the increasing union of the affinoid polydiscs of radii r ∈ |K°°_∞|; over each such Tate algebra B_r the base change is flat over B_r⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩ by affinoid-rational-flat, and every maximal ideal of the Noetherian ring A_j0 is a point of some polydisc.

items.name: Freeness of the special fibre of the Noetherian stage
items.statement: A°_j0⟨T^(1/p^j), U⟩/(ϖ_ik U − f_ik, ϖ_j) = A°_j0⟨T^(1/p^j), U⟩/(f_ik, ϖ_j) ≅ (A°_j0/ϖ_j)[T^(1/p^j), U]/(T^(1/p^k) − g_k), which is free over A°_j0/ϖ_j.
items.note: The congruences f_ik^(p^k) ≡ f_i ≡ T − g ≡ (T^(1/p^k) − g_k)^(p^k) modulo ϖ′ and (15) give f_ik ≡ T^(1/p^k) − g_k modulo ϖ_j. With g_k T-free modulo ϖ_j (noetherian-stage-model), T^(1/p^k) − g_k is monic of degree p^(j−k) in T^(1/p^j).

items.name: Faithful flatness of the Noetherian stage
items.statement: A_j0⟨T^(1/p^j)⟩{f_ik/ϖ_ik}_(≤1) is faithfully flat over A°_j0.
items.note: Flatness from flatness-by-fibres with generic-fibre-flat and special-fibre-free. Faithfulness: A°_j0 is local and the closed fibre is k[T^(1/p^j), U]/f̄_ik, which is nonzero because f̄_ik^(p^k) ≡ T − ḡ is not a unit.

items.name: Flatness over a filtered colimit of rings
items.statement: Let R_∞ = colim_j R_j be a filtered colimit of rings with flat transition maps, and M an R_∞-module that is flat (respectively faithfully flat, when M is an R_∞-algebra) over every R_j. Then M is flat (respectively faithfully flat) over R_∞.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.5.2, p.81 (“il en est de même de colim_j … sur colim_j A°_j0 = A°_∞0, c'est-à-dire sur chaque A°_j0”); §2.3, p.78
items.note: A finitely generated ideal of R_∞ is extended from some R_j, and Tor_1^(R_∞)(R_∞ ⊗ N, M) = Tor_1^(R_j)(N, M) because R_∞ is R_j-flat. For faithfulness, 1 ∈ m_∞ M would already hold at a finite stage.

items.name: Coherence of a flat colimit of Noetherian rings
items.statement: A filtered colimit of Noetherian rings with flat transition maps is a coherent ring.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 2.6.1, p.82, citing Bourbaki AC I §2 ex. 12
items.note: Applied to A°_∞0 = colim_j A°_j0 with finite flat transition maps.

items.name: Finitely presented ideals descend along a flat colimit
items.statement: Let R_∞ = colim_j R_j be a filtered colimit with flat transition maps and I a finitely generated ideal of R_∞. Then I = I_j R_∞ ≅ I_j ⊗_(R_j) R_∞ for an ideal I_j of some R_j.
items.locator: Proof of Corollary 2.6.1, p.82 (“I est un idéal de présentation finie, donc provient d'un idéal I_j de l'un des A°_j0”)
items.note: Take generators in some R_j; flatness of R_∞ over R_j makes I_j ⊗ R_∞ → R_∞ injective. In the application I is the annihilator of a finitely presented module over the coherent ring A°_∞0.

items.name: Annihilators under flat base change
items.statement: Let R be a Noetherian ring, M a finite R-module and S a flat R-algebra. Then Ann_S(M ⊗_R S) = Ann_R(M) S.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 1.1.2, p.76 (“Par platitude, on a JS = Ann M_S”)
items.note: M is finitely presented, so Ann(M) is the kernel of R → End_R(M) ⊆ M^n, and flat base change preserves this kernel.

items.name: Tor commutes with filtered colimits
items.statement: For a ring R, an R-module P and a filtered system of R-modules (N_α), Tor_i^R(P, colim N_α) ≅ colim Tor_i^R(P, N_α) for every i.
items.locator: Remark after Lemma A.1.1, p.89 (“les colimites filtrantes commutent aux Tor par exactitude”)
items.note: Mathlib has Tor as a derived functor (CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Tor.lean) but not this comparison at the pin.
